summary: A money or number KPI: a caption, a big formatted value (thousands grouping, a prefix or suffix such as a currency, decimals, optional K / M abbreviation, 7 digits and more) that shrinks to fit its width, and an optional change in percent with a drawn up or down arrow and its sign, green when good and red when bad. Read as one item: "Revenue, $1,234,567, up 4.2 percent".

value.doc: The number: a literal, a "@variable" or an expression. Floats hold 7 significant digits exactly (integers up to 16,777,216); beyond that the last digits are approximate

caption.doc: Small muted line over the value ("Revenue this month"), literal text; also the start of the description

prefix.doc: Before the number, no space added: "$", "€", "£"

suffix.doc: After the number, as written: " €", " kWh", "%"

decimals.doc: Digits after the decimal point (2 for cents)

grouping.doc: Thousands separator: comma 1,234,567.89; period 1.234.567,89; space 1 234 567,89; none 1234567.89

abbreviate.doc: Show 1,000 and over as 1.2K and 1,000,000 and over as 3.4M (one decimal); under 1,000 the value keeps `decimals`. The description still reads the full value

change.doc: Change in percent, signed (4.2 for +4.2 %): a literal or a "@variable". Its sign picks the arrow, the sign and the colour (exactly 0: a muted flat arrow, read "unchanged"); omitted, or a literal 0, no change line

changeDecimals.doc: Digits after the point in the change

invert.doc: true when a fall is good (costs, churn): a rise turns red and a fall green

fontSize.doc: Value text size in dp (the canvas is 1.25 × this tall for the value, plus 18 dp for the caption and 22 dp for the change)

align.doc: Where the lines sit in the width the component fills

label.doc: What a screen reader says in place of the caption, literal text: the value and the change are still spoken after it ("Sales today, $1,234, up 4.2 percent")

pitfalls: Everything is drawn on one canvas (drawTextAnchored), so a screen reader hears one item: an empty box over the canvas, after it, carries textMerge(caption, value, "up" or "down", the change, "percent"). The word is cut from "updownunchanged" with textSubtext inside the canvas, which is why the description sits on a box after it: "@name" resolves only once the name is defined

Numbers are textFromFloat with flags 7 (no leading padding, trailing zeros kept so cents read .50) + 16 (group by three) + the separator style (64 period, 128 space): 23, 87, 151. whole is 9 digits; a float carries about 7 significant digits, so 12,345,678.91 prints as 12,345,679.00, and cents on 7-digit amounts are wrong (the C++ player draws 1,284,530.25 as 1,284,530.30 while the description says .25): show amounts of a million and more without cents (decimals 0) or abbreviated

The value is measured (textMeasure) and drawn under a scale of min(1, width / measured), so 7 or 9 digits shrink to fit a narrow tile instead of being cut off (StatTile stops at 6 digits). It fills its parent's width: in a row, give it a weighted box

abbreviate draws three texts (full, K, M) and shows one with paint alpha: k = step(|v|, 999.5) − m, m = step(|v|, 999999.5); the abbreviated number is value / (1 + 999 k + 999999 m) with one decimal, so 999,960 shows 1000.0K

The change line is three copies (the up arrow and +x% in success, the down arrow and −x% in error, a flat muted arrow and 0.0%) switched by paint alpha up = step(change, 0), dn = step(−change, 0), flat = 1 − up − dn; the spoken word (up, down, unchanged) is cut from "updownunchanged" with the same three. In mono both colours are white (black on mono-light): the arrow's direction and the sign carry the meaning
The prefix goes before the sign: a negative value with prefix "$" prints $-1,234; put the minus in your caption or use suffix instead
Drawn text has no bold and does not follow the system font scale
